dedupe_keys.name: improving sediment monitoring strategies based on analysing heat transfer processes in sewer pipes

description: Manuel Regueiro-Picallo and colleagues at Universidade da Coruña describe a developed modelling method for locating sewer-sediment monitors. Sewer-network hydrodynamics identify potential accumulation locations, while network thermodynamics simulate temperature patterns from which sediment depth can be estimated. The source states that combining these analyses supports selection of monitoring-device locations. This record describes the network-level deployment method; the related MONTSE record concerns local temperature-to-depth inference and experimental validation. Zenodo supplies the conference paper freely under CC BY 4.0. The native abstract does not identify a named catchment, spatial discretisation, input file format or quantitative performance metric. Code access and its licence are unknown. A limitation is that the brief metadata establish the implemented modelling role but not a reproducible software package or deployment performance in an operational sewer. No paper body or model files were read.
